title: Candidate integration lightning 10-day retention runbook
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a lightweight, battle-tested runbook for rapidly integrating new hires into small product engineering pods with a 10-day high-touch sprint designed to maximize retention signals. It sits between the full 30/90 onboarding playbooks and ad-hoc buddy checklists — intended for hires who need an accelerated but sustainable ramp (early-career ICs, internal transfers, contractors-to-perm).

Scope and assumptions:
- Target audience: hiring managers, onboarding coordinators, buddy/mentor pairs, recruiting ops.
- Assumes standard preboarding (access, laptop, HR forms) completed before Day 0.
- Not a replacement for team-specific technical onboarding; it focuses on socialization, early wins, signal detection, and automated handoffs.
- Timebox: focused first 10 calendar days, with clear handoff into 30/90 plan on Day 11.

Top-level goals (10-day sprint):
1) Produce one measurable, merged small contribution (bugfix, doc, test) by Day 8.
2) Complete 3 structured social touchpoints (manager 1:1, buddy check-in, team sync).
3) Verify access and productive environment with automated validation script.
4) Capture early sentiment & risk signals in the retention dashboard.

Day-by-day playbook (concise):
- Day 0 (preboarding done): welcome email (template), Slack intro, calendar block for buddy and first-week schedule, run automated env check (link to script), add to retention dashboard.
- Day 1: orientation 30m (people ops), manager 30m expectations, buddy walkthrough 60–90m (repo readme, dev env, tiny issue assigned). Ship first commit: doc or tiny fix.
- Day 2: paired debugging session (1h) + self-study block for core tech. Automated permissions audit. Short pulse survey (2 questions).
- Day 3: product context lunch w/PM or engineering lead (30m) + async knowledge snippets shared. Update onboarding notes.
- Day 4: mini-project planning session (mentor + new hire) to scope the Day 8 deliverable. Add acceptance criteria to the issue.
- Day 5: review and feedback loop; code review walkthrough. Manager catch-up (15m): blockers and clarity.
- Day 6: focus day for workstream; automated shadow analytics run to detect if new hire is stuck (no commits, failing env checks). If flagged, escalate to mentor.
- Day 7: canary merge attempt for the deliverable; patch and iterate with reviewer.
- Day 8: ship deliverable; retrospective 20m with buddy and manager to capture learnings.
- Day 9: career conversation starter (manager 30m): map 30/90 expectations, signals, and growth areas.
- Day 10: retention pulse + handoff package prepared (links, tickets, mentor notes) and added to team-runbook; schedule 30-day check in.

Key templates (copy/modify from linked artifacts):
- Welcome email (short, includes first tasks + buddy contact)
- Slack intro template (role, pronouns, 1–2 fun facts)
- 2-question pulse survey: 1) How confident are you to make a small contribution? (1–5) 2) Any blockers we should solve in the next 24h? (free text)
- Day 8 ship checklist: PR linked, reviewer assigned, changelog note, CI green, reviewer thumbs / signoff.

Automation and signals (practical):
- Environment validator: runs on Day 0 & Day 2, checks dev server access, docker/container run, CI token presence. Report posted to #people-ops-onboard.
- Retention dashboard: aggregates pulse surveys, env-check failures, number of merged commits, and sentiment keywords from 1:1 notes (privacy: only aggregated/opt-in fields stored).
- Stuck detection heuristics: no repo activity + open local errors + >48h blocker -> auto-notify mentor and recruiting ops.

Interview/handoff rubric (for interviewer → manager transitions):
- Short summary to include in offer folder: candidate strengths (3 bullets), top risk areas (2 bullets), cultural match evidence (1–2 short examples), recommended first tasks (2–3).
- Standard language for scorecards: what ‘needs onboarding attention’ looks like vs. acceptable to start.

Retention signal triggers (manual + automated):
- RED: expresses strong uncertainty in Day 2 pulse OR env check failed twice OR manager reports missed meetings. Action: mandatory 24h escalation to hiring manager + people ops check-in.
- AMBER: low confidence score (2–3) OR delayed first commit. Action: buddy deep-dive and micro-plan for 48h.
- GREEN: pulse >=4, first commit merged, attended social sync. Continue normal 30/90.

Manager checklist (things to do within 10 days):
- Introduce success metrics for first 30 days (1–3 measurable outcomes).
- Add new hire to oncall rotation only after Day 30 and manager signoff.
- Provide feedback within 48 hours of first PR review.
- Document role-specific access or hardware needs early.

Buddy/mentor quick guide (what to cover):
- Day 1: local setup + quick path to first tiny PR.
- Ongoing: timeboxed pairing sessions, codebase orientation map, 1–2 sample walkthroughs.
- Notes: avoid over-mentoring (enable autonomy). Keep check-ins to 30m.

Escalation matrix (who to ping):
- Immediate blocker (access/infra): infra-oncall or platform-eng Slack + #people-ops-onboard.
- Match/culture concerns: people-ops lead (Priya Shah).
- Hiring calibration problems: recruiting manager + hiring manager sync.

Metrics to track (minimum):
- % of hires with first merged contribution <=8 days
- Day 2 and Day 10 pulse average by cohort
- % of hires flagged RED within 10 days
- 30/90 retention conversion rate for lightning cohort vs baseline

Open questions / tradeoffs (notes to self):
- Should we require a merged PR by Day 5 for contractor-to-perm? (pro: early filter; con: pressure.)
- How do we balance privacy vs useful signal capture in retention dashboard? Need legal input.
- Does the buddy allocation scale for hiring surges? Potentially use a rotating pool with 2-hour blocks.

TODOs (short run):
- [ ] Move welcome email template to github/hr-templates and link it in Confluence. (Marco)
- [ ] Implement env-validator as a GitHub Action (infra + 1 engineer volunteer).
- [ ] Draft legal note on retention dashboard data handling (Priya).
- [ ] Pilot with two pods in September (owners: Aisha + Jordan).

Quick wins and pragmatic tips from pilots:
- Make the first task review a doc/README edit — lower friction than code and still validates flow.
- Timebox pairing to 30–60m; too-long sessions burn mentors.
- Use a single Slack thread per hire to centralize history; archive to the hire folder at Day 11.

Appendix (copyable snippets):
- Welcome email subject: Welcome to Redwood — your Day 1 checklist
- Slack intro: "Hi all — please welcome NAME, joining as ROLE on TEAM. Buddy: @buddy. Drop a tip or hello!"
- Day 1 tiny issue description example: "Fix typo and expand README section on local dev flow (steps, env vars, common gotchas)."

Footnote: This runbook is intentionally prescriptive but lightweight. Treat it as an experiment and iterate after every pilot cohort. Capture notes in the retention dashboard and the people-ops handbook.
